row.title: Rename Canopy to Trov, with the new logo
row.body:
## What this is

The rename and the new logo, split out of the multitenancy branch (`claude/sharp-hawking-m0jgdp`) so they can ship now. No multitenancy schema or code is in here.

- **Canopy → Trov** across the app, landing page, emails, OAuth consent pages, MCP server name and tool descriptions, README / AGENTS / CLAUDE.md, and `canopy.css` → `trov.css`.
- **Plugin** moves to `plugins/trov` (0.7.0); the `canopy` skill becomes `trov`.
- **Tokens**: new ones mint as `trov_mcp_` / `trov_oat_` / `trov_ort_`; `canopy_*` tokens still resolve. Browser `canopy.*` keys move to `trov.*` once at boot.
- **Email**: every address is `hello@trov.dev`; migration `0041_trov_name` moves the default sender to `Trov <hello@trov.dev>` and leaves an admin-edited one alone.
- **Terms and Privacy pages** at `/terms` and `/privacy`, linked from the landing footer (the rename commit builds on them).
- **New logo**: `shared/mark.ts` holds the mark and its two purples (`#616ACB` light, `#8991D7` dark, via a `--mark` token). It replaces the three bars in the sidebar, sign-in, landing, legal and OAuth pages, the tab icon (`favicon.svg`, `favicon.ico` in place of `favicon-32.png`, an apple-touch icon) and the email banner (drawn as table cells, since Gmail strips SVG).

Deliberately not renamed: the `canopy.saplinglearn.com` domain, the Worker / D1 / R2 names, the `canopy/*` commit statuses and user-agents in Sapling's contracts, the stored `tickets.source = 'canopy'`, and the HMAC labels.

## Before merging

Merging deploys to production, and it applies `0041_trov_name`.

- [ ] `trov.dev` is a verified Resend sending domain and `hello@trov.dev` receives mail. Until then every digest, invite and welcome mail would fail.
- [ ] Everyone reinstalls the plugin afterwards: `/plugin uninstall canopy`, `/plugin marketplace add AndresL230/trov`, `/plugin install trov@trov`, then `/mcp` → trov → Authenticate.
- [ ] The Get Started guide screenshots still say "Canopy" (`scripts/capture-guide.mjs` re-captures them).
- [ ] Legal pages name the operator as "Andres Lopez".

The migration keeps the number `0041` so the multitenancy branch's `0037`–`0040` do not need renumbering. It only touches `notification_settings.from_address` and does not depend on them.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` passes; `npm run build:web` passes.
- `npm test`: 160 files, 2,699 tests pass. The command still exits 1 because of four unhandled `ArtifactError` rejections from `src/tools/artifacts-agent.ts`; the same four fail CI on the multitenancy branch and the code is untouched here.

row.title: Organizations: multi-tenant Trov, superadmin Platform area, org settings and keys
row.body:
## What this is

Trov becomes multi-tenant. A platform superadmin can add an organization and name its admin; that admin signs in, invites their team, connects a repository and configures their own keys. Nothing is shared between organizations.

This branch also contains the rename and logo from #92. Merge #92 first if you want that to ship on its own; this PR then shows only the multitenancy work.

**Do not merge yet.** Merging deploys to production and applies ten migrations, two of which rebuild 20 tables. The owner steps and the open decisions are below and in `HANDOFF.md`.

## What changed

- **Data layer** — every query runs through `src/data/` with an explicit org; a static test (`test/data-layer.static.test.ts`) fails on raw database access anywhere else, and on a tenant statement that does not name its org.
- **Organizations** — create, switch, invite by GitHub login or e-mail (the invitation is mailed), roles (owner / admin / member), suspension. The app lives at `/o/<slug>/`; old links still open for a person in one org.
- **Org settings** (admins) — Members, Repositories, Environments, and Integrations: per-org credentials that are envelope-encrypted, write-only, with Test connection, rotation and an audit history. A setup checklist walks a new org's admin through it.
- **Platform** (superadmin, at `/platform/` and in the sidebar) — add an organization and assign its admin, add another owner, suspend, per-person org limits, superadmins, audit, and usage: sizes, activity and per-day series per org.
- **MCP** — a token or OAuth connection is bound to one organization; the consent page asks which when a person is in several.
- **Background work** — cron, digests and webhooks run per org with that org's stored credentials. `POST /webhook/github/:hookId` is the per-repo webhook; the existing `/webhook/github` keeps delivering for SaplingLearn.
- **Sign-in** — any GitHub account can sign in; Google still needs an invitation matching a provider-verified e-mail. The `ADMIN_LOGINS` allowlist is gone; the org role is the only admin.
- **Numbers** — tickets and handoffs are addressed by their number within the org, so a new org's first ticket is `#1`. SaplingLearn's numbers equal its existing ids.
- **Abuse limits** — per-person daily caps on invites, test sends, notification-address changes and avatar uploads; every mail leaves from the platform address with a sanitised org name.

Operator guide: `docs/architecture/organizations.md`. Architecture: `docs/architecture/data-layer.md`, `docs/architecture/abuse-limits.md`. Release notes: 0.18 in `web/src/releases.ts`.

## Before a production deploy — owner steps

The full ordered list is `HANDOFF.md` › "OWNER STEPS". In short:

- [ ] Take a D1 export and note the Time Travel bookmark; run `node scripts/mt/verify-migration.mjs` on the export. It has only been run on a local fixture. If it reports any ticket or handoff whose number differs from its id, stop.
- [ ] Apply migrations `0037`–`0043`, `0045`, `0046`, `0047` (there is no `0044`).
- [ ] Set `TROV_KEK` (`openssl rand -base64 32`, then `wrangler secret put TROV_KEK`) and keep a copy. Losing it loses every org's stored credentials.
- [ ] Confirm the Worker is on Workers Paid: the cron budgets 900 subrequests per run.
- [ ] Enter SaplingLearn's credentials on Org settings › Integrations. Until then it falls back to the existing Worker secrets.
- [ ] Everything in #92's checklist (Resend domain for `hello@trov.dev`, plugin reinstall).

## Decisions that are the owner's, not the code's

1. **Mail to strangers.** Once mail is live, any org's admin can have Trov send an invitation to any address, 50 a day per person. `wrangler.toml` has notifications in local mode today.
2. **Open sign-in.** Identity pinning for existing GitHub identities only takes effect at each member's next sign-in; invites by GitHub login go to whoever holds that login; one Gemini key and one cron budget are shared by every org. See `abuse-limits.md` › Residu

cases.rationale: Multi-tenant organizations: the data model, addresses and settings change underneath everyone.

row.title: fix(mywork): PR cards are structured-only — drop the legacy pr_summaries.summary
row.body:
## Problem
On My Work → **Previous activity**, a PR card rendered a raw **"Summary"** excerpt row whenever the capture-time Workers-AI summary fell back to the excerpt (i.e. `what/why/impact` all null — as happened to PR #321). A prose "Summary" row is the **issue/todo** surface; PR cards should be **What changed / Why / Impact** only.

## Change — remove `pr.summary` end-to-end
- **render** (`web/src/render.ts`): `prActivityCard` renders `What changed` / `Why` / `Impact` only. A PR with no structured summary shows a **"No summary recorded"** placeholder — the raw excerpt is never rendered.
- **DTO/query**: drop `summary` from `MyWorkPr` (`shared/dashboard.ts`) and the `getMyWork` PR `SELECT`/mapping (`src/tools/mywork.ts`).
- **store** (`src/tools/summarize.ts`): `storePrSummary` no longer mirrors `what`→`summary`; a PR's excerpt fallback is now a **content-less marker** row (`model='excerpt'`, null structured columns) that Sync retries.
- **schema**: `0019_drop_pr_summary.sql` drops the (NOT NULL) `pr_summaries.summary` column. `issue_summaries` is untouched — **issues keep their prose summary**.
- **seed + tests + CLAUDE.md** updated.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` clean · `npm run build:web` clean
- Full suite green: **53 files / 418 tests** (migration 0019 applies cleanly in the test D1).

## ⚠️ Deploy ordering
`pr_summaries.summary` is still `NOT NULL` in prod and the new INSERT omits it, so apply the migration **before** deploying:
```
npm run db:migrate:remote   # applies 0019 (deploy does NOT auto-apply remote migrations)
npm run deploy
```

row.title: Embedded checkout: pay for Pro inside Trov (off by default)
row.body:
Buying Pro can happen on a Trov page, in the same bannered card as the rest of signing up, instead of on Stripe's hosted page. **It ships switched off**: nothing changes for a buyer until `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` is set.

## What it adds

- `/billing/checkout`: Stripe's embedded form mounted in the first-run card, then on to the existing "Payment received" step. The webhook is still the only thing that fulfils a purchase.
- One switch, `BillingConfig.embedded`: on only when `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` is a `pk_…` key whose mode matches the secret key's and the API base is real Stripe. Empty (the default) or mismatched means the hosted redirect, exactly as today.
- A reload resumes the same session; a paid one goes to the confirmation; an expired one offers to start again.
- If Stripe.js cannot load, the page says so and offers the hosted checkout for the same purchase.
- Stripe.js is loaded from `js.stripe.com` on that page only.
- Upstream error text is scrubbed of client secrets before it is logged.

No migration, no new secret, no cron change.

## Not verified against real Stripe

Everything in a browser ran against a local fake of Stripe.js. Only a real test can show: that the form mounts with a real key at the pinned API version (`2024-06-20`), how it fits the card in light, dark and at phone width, 3-D Secure and the real return, and that Stripe accepts the adjustable seat count and tax parameters on an embedded session. Stripe's API reference lists no restriction on them and confirms `ui_mode: "embedded"`, `return_url`, and that `success_url` / `cancel_url` are not allowed.

**Before turning it on:** follow "First real test" in `docs/architecture/billing.md` (Stripe test mode, your own keys in `.dev.vars`, `stripe listen` for the webhook).

## To turn it on, later

Paste the publishable key into `wrangler.toml` `[vars]` as `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` and merge. To turn it off, empty it.

## Tests

`npm test` 229 files / 4,567 tests and `npm run typecheck` green locally.

row.title: Add Handoffs and the Prompt Library
row.body:
Adds **Handoffs** (addressed messages from one session to the next) and the **Prompt Library** (versioned, reusable prompts), end to end: D1 storage, session-cookie routes, MCP tools, Claude Code skills and the SPA screens ported from the Claude Design `Canopy.dc.html` (project `2c8cfa50`). The same port brings a tabbed Maintenance (Unplaced / Identity / People) and a Docs › New doc form.

Verified: `npm run typecheck` clean, `npx vitest run` 123 files / 1787 tests green, `npm run build:web` ok, and the write flows driven in a browser against `wrangler dev` (send → claim → second claim 409 → expire; save prompt → publish; FTS search; handoff → Promote to doc → staged v1 proposal in Review).

## Migration
- `0028_handoffs_prompts.sql` — `handoffs` (INTEGER id, `context` JSON, inline prompt both-or-neither via CHECK, `expires_at`; indexes `(recipient, status)`, `(sender, created_at)`), `prompts`, `prompt_versions`, and `prompts_fts` (standalone FTS5 like `tickets_fts`, kept at each prompt's latest version by triggers on both tables). **Needs `npm run db:migrate:remote` before deploy.**

## Routes (session cookie, errors are `{ error }`)
- `GET /api/handoffs?box=mine|me|anyone|sent` → `{ handoffs }`, newest first
- `GET /api/handoffs/:id` → `{ handoff }`
- `POST /api/handoffs` `{ recipient?, body, context?, prompt? }` → `{ ok, handoff }` — sender is the principal; recipient `anyone` or a known handle; body ≤ 32 KB; expires in 7 days; writes a feed entry; replay-safe via `processed_items` when the request carries a session id + item index
- `POST /api/handoffs/:id/claim` `{ session }` → `{ ok, handoff }` or 409 `handoff is <status>` — one conditional `UPDATE … WHERE id=? AND status='pending'` with the permission check in the same statement
- `POST /api/handoffs/:id/expire` → `{ ok, handoff }` or 409 — sender or recipient only
- `GET /api/prompts?q=&tags=a,b&sort=updated_desc|updated_asc` → `{ prompts }` (FTS `q`, tags AND)
- `GET /api/prompts/:slug` → `{ prompt }`, `GET /api/prompts/:slug/versions` → `{ versions }` newest first
- `POST /api/prompts` `{ slug, base_slug?, title, tags, body, status?, summary? }` → `{ ok, prompt }` — upsert on `base_slug || slug`, always appends a version; humans default to `draft`, may publish and rename
- `POST /api/prompts/:slug/tags` `{ tags }`, `POST /api/prompts/:slug/publish` `{ version }` (409 `not staged`)
- `POST /api/docs/propose` `{ title, section, space, body, summary?, slug? }` → `{ ok, proposal }` — through the existing gate (`ingestDocProposal`) as a new v1; an existing slug is 409, an off-vocab section 400

Cron: `expireDueHandoffs` runs as its own guarded arm on every `*/10` repo tick (D1 only, no subrequests).

## MCP tools (principal = bearer owner)
- `send_handoff` — "Leave a handoff for the next session: where a task stands when you stop mid-way (context running out, switching person, ending the session). Send exactly ONE per session and tell the person its id as #N. `recipient` is a person handle, or omit it for 'anyone' (the first session to claim it gets it). Keep `body` under 300 words — its first line is the title, the rest says where things stand. ALWAYS fill `context` with the fixed shape { repo, branch, task, done[], next[], files[] }: repo from the git remote (owner/name), branch from HEAD, task as one line, done/next as short items, files from `git diff --name-only` against main. Long step-by-step instructions for the claiming session go in `prompt.body` (with a `prompt.title`), not in body. Pass your session id as `session` so a retry does not send twice. Returns { id, url }."
- `list_handoffs` — "List handoffs waiting for you. With no `box`, returns the PENDING ones left for you ('me') plus open 'anyone' handoffs from other people — call this at session start and tell the person what is waiting; never claim one without asking. box: 'me' (left for you), 'anyone' (open to all, from others), 'mine' (sent by or left for you), 'sent' (what you sent — the only box that incl

row.title: feat: Google sign-in and person-centric identity
row.body:
Brings the Google sign-in / person-centric identity work (PR #41) into `main`. #41 was merged into `feat/email-theme` rather than `main`, so the work has been sitting one branch short of the default branch — and was never deployed. This is that missing hop.

## What lands

- **Identity model (`0023_persons.sql`)** — `persons` / `identities` / `invites`; a person owns N provider identities. `sessions` and `mcp_tokens` repoint from `user` to `person`; `users` and `people` are dropped.
- **Google provider** — PKCE authorize, code exchange, JWKS-verified ID token; the shared sign-in fork (`completeSignIn`) plus link mode, so a Google identity can attach to an existing person.
- **Invites** — invite store, admin invite routes, invite email through the existing delivery gate.
- **Web** — "Continue with Google", not-invited card, onboarding screen, Settings › Profile (color, sign-in methods), Maintenance › People, colored person chips, handle text carrying the person's color.
- **Self-service handle rename** — atomic multi-table rewrite.
- **Readers/writers** resolve through `identities` + `persons`; `Principal` carries `handle`.

## Also in this PR

- `fix(test): stamp the retry fixture relative to now` — three `retryFailed` tests in `test/notifications.cron.test.ts` were failing. Root cause was not the identity work: the fixture stamped `created_at` with an absolute date (`2026-09-11T12:00Z`) while `retryFailed` bounds rows to `now - 48h`, so from 2026-09-13T12:00Z on the row aged out and the job never saw it. Two sibling tests were also passing vacuously; a mutation check confirms the unsubscribe gate is genuinely covered again.
- `Merge branch 'main'` — resolves the conflicts with PR #38 (main-pane scroll preservation), which this branch never saw. Union of both tsconfig include/exclude lists (every test importing `web/src` must appear in both), both import groups in `web/src/main.ts`, and `test/render.scroll.test.ts`'s `Me` fixture updated to the persons shape. Verified the scroll fix is intact end to end: `captureScroll`/`restoreScroll` still bracket the `mount.innerHTML = render(state)` swap, and `render.ts` still emits the `id="cnpy-main"` anchor.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 682/683 (the one remaining local failure is the documented `GEMINI_API_KEY`-in-`.dev.vars` leak; 43/43 in `test/summarize.test.ts` with the key absent).
- `npm run typecheck` — exit 0.

## ⚠️ Merging this IS a production deploy, and the migration must go first

Cloudflare Workers Builds is connected to this repo: a push to `main` builds and **deploys production** (the build on merge `2531683` started 2026-09-13T09:18:41Z; a deployment landed at 09:18:37Z — same pairing on `42cb84d`). Feature-branch pushes build but do not touch production.

`0023_persons.sql` is **not yet applied** to the prod D1, and it is not additive: it rebuilds `sessions` / `mcp_tokens` / `notification_outbox_bodies` and **drops `users` and `people`**. So:

- Merge before migrating → the new code goes live against a schema with no `persons` / `identities`: sign-in, sessions and My Work all fail.
- Migrate before merging → the currently-live Worker loses `users` / `people` and breaks until the new code is live.

Either way there is a short outage window, so run them back to back, off-hours: `npm run db:migrate:remote`, then get the new code live (merging here, or `npm run deploy` from the merged tree for the shortest window). Sessions should survive — 0023 carries `sessions.id` across and handle = old login.

`GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` are already set as prod secrets ✅. `ADMIN_LOGINS` becomes `AndresL230,andres` to carry the handle rename.

row.title: Emails: fit a phone (the card is fluid, not 680px)
row.body:
Every Trov email was 680px wide on a phone. The card was a `width="680"` table; a table is at least as wide as its `width`, so `max-width:100%` never applied and the client scaled the mail down or scrolled it sideways.

- The card is fluid up to 680px (`emailCardOpen`): `width="100%"` with `max-width`. Outlook ignores `max-width`, so it alone gets a fixed-width wrapper through a conditional comment.
- Under 520px (`EMAIL_MOBILE_CSS`): the page gutter tightens, the banner's faint mark makes room for the headline, and the headline steps down from 25px to 22px. A client that drops `<style>` still gets a card that fits.

## Measured (rendered samples in an iframe)
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Page width in a 375px viewport | 712px | 375px |
| Card | 680px | 355px |
| Elements past the right edge | 40+ | 0 |

Same at 320px. Not seen: a real mail client (Gmail app, Apple Mail, Outlook). No screenshot was possible in this session; the numbers above are from layout measurements.

## Tests
`npm run typecheck` clean; full suite 4,264 passing before the four width tests were rewritten; those files pass now.

row.title: fix(cron): weekly digest trigger uses SUN,MON (Cloudflare weekdays are 1-7)
row.body:
The PR #34 deploy uploaded the Worker but failed on the schedules step: Cloudflare's cron weekdays field accepts `1-7` (1 = Sunday) or `SUN`–`SAT`, never `0`, so `"0 * * * 0,1"` was rejected. Switched the weekly candidate trigger to `"0 * * * SUN,MON"` in `wrangler.toml`, `src/notifications/cron.ts` and CLAUDE.md. Tests pin the string from `wrangler.toml`.

Production has already been repaired out of band: migrations 0021/0022 were applied remotely (the merged code needs `users.email`; login was failing until then) and the corrected triggers were pushed with `wrangler triggers deploy`. Merging this makes CI agree with what is live.
